label: Centrally planned economy
description: Output is set by capacity, not demand. The Plan divides it between investment, defence, civil government and exports; households get the rest. Everyone has a job and prices are fixed, so excess demand shows up as shortages and unspendable savings, not inflation.

capital_share.note: Capital's share in the production function, as for the United States.

tfp_growth.note: Growth of total factor productivity in 1949. Western estimates for the 1950s run near 2%, helped by post-war recovery and borrowed technology.

tfp_growth_decay.note: Yearly rate at which productivity growth fades. Western estimates show Soviet productivity growth falling from about 2% in the 1950s to near zero by the late 1970s: the planned economy's growing difficulty in innovating and allocating efficiently.

labour_force_growth.note: Yearly growth of the Soviet labour force in the 1950s. A placeholder until pops and demography drive it in Phase 3.

sector_capacity_ceiling.note: How far (%) one industry can be pushed above normal capacity by 'storming'.

overhang_spend_rate.note: Share of the savings overhang households try to spend each year when goods appear in the shops.

income_balancing.note: Share of any gap between households' money incomes and the consumer goods the Plan provides that the planners close each year: through compulsory state loans (which took several per cent of wages until 1957), price rises and wage controls.

investment_allocation_sensitivity.note: How far planners steer investment towards bottlenecks on top of the Plan's priorities, through the 'material balances' that matched supplies to needs. An industry 10% more stretched than average gets 40% more than its planned share.

utilisation_smoothing.note: Weight on the latest quarter when planners judge how stretched an industry is.

surge_import_share.note: Share of a shortage met by extra imports. Low: the USSR had little hard currency and preferred autarky.

surge_import_cap.note: Extra imports can cover at most this share of a product's normal home use in a quarter.

ration_weight_consumption.note: Households are cut first when goods run short: queues and empty shelves.

ration_weight_investment.note: Plan investment is protected, though projects still overrun.

ration_weight_inventories.note: Stockbuilding is cut when goods are short.

ration_weight_government.note: Defence and state orders have first call on output.

ration_weight_exports.note: Export commitments, largely to the bloc, are protected.

arms_race_reaction.note: Points of GDP the Soviets add to defence for each point by which the rival spends above what the Plan expected (and cut when it spends less).

max_defence_share.note: Most of GDP the planners will give defence in peacetime.

min_defence_share.note: Least of GDP the planners will give defence, however little the rival spends.
